title: Introduce stable throughput watcher and opportunistic burst bridger
author: Marta Rivera
rollout_strategy: canary 10% pools -> 50% after 24h -> global after 72h pending metrics
description:
Motivation: We frequently observe transient latency spikes and capacity thrash when multiple tenants simultaneously increase throughput. Existing autoscaling reacts to windowed utilization which can overreact to short bursts or underreact when sustained low-but-rising demand occurs. This PR adds two cooperating pieces: (1) a Stable Throughput Watcher (STW) that computes a drift-aware cumulative utilization estimator and emits stable SLO-driven throughput targets, and (2) an Opportunistic Burst Bridger that safely borrows ephemeral warm capacity for short, high-variance bursts without changing tenant commitments.

Summary of changes: 
- Implemented pkg/autoscaler/watcher.go: drift-aware exponential quantile estimator with hysteresis and noise floor filtering. The estimator uses per-tenant rolling windows using commit-aligned buckets to avoid cross-tenant leakage.
- Added pkg/autoscaler/bridge.go: a lightweight bridge that routes short-window burst traffic into an opportunistic warm pool and tags requests with a borrow token so accounting/telemetry reconciles borrowed capacity. Bridge enforces per-tenant max-bridge-slices and decays borrow credits.
- Telemetry: integration with cmd/telemetry/reporter to emit cumulative_util_q{p50,p90,p99}, borrow_credit_balance, and bridge_fail_rate metrics. These are exported to Prometheus with labels for pool, tenant, and rollout_phase.
- Config and deployment: helm chart updates to allow separate sizing for opportunistic warm pools and new feature flags to enable STW/bridge per-region.
- Docs: design doc under docs/design/fleet-throughput-watcher.md describing algorithm, safety invariants, and rollout checklist.

Design notes: 
- The STW estimator favors conservative growth: it only increases throughput targets when both (a) quantile drift exceeds configured hysteresis and (b) sustained for a configured stabilization window. Decreases are faster but bounded to avoid oscillation.
- The bridge borrows only from a pre-sized warm pool and uses a token ledger to ensure borrowed capacity is repaid (credit decay + positive reinforcement when slack observed). If bridge borrow rate increases past safety thresholds, traffic is routed back to the base path and an event is emitted.
- Accounting: borrowed requests are marked in the tracing span and contribute to borrowed_tokens metric. Billing/usage pipeline is unchanged but instrumentation allows us to generate reconciled utilization reports for capacity planning.

Testing & validation: 
- Unit tests for estimator edge cases and token ledger (pkg/autoscaler/watch_test.go).
- Integration scenario tests using integration/tests/fleet_sim_fixture.yaml that drive synthetic multi-tenant diurnal + spike traces. Verified no SLA regressions at 99th p95 token latency and lower overall cost compared to baseline reactive autoscaler in medium variance traces (~11% lower GPU-seconds over 6h simulation).
- Load bench: microbench for bridge path latency shows median added latency < 2ms and p99 < 12ms under synthetic burst load.

Rollout plan: enable feature flag in canary region (us-east-1) for 10% of pools, monitor cumulative_util_q and borrow_credit_balance dashboards, abort if bridge_fail_rate > 1% sustained for 10m or if tenant p99 latency increases > 5% over baseline. Gradual expansion steps described in docs/design/fleet-throughput-watcher.md.

Backward compatibility and safety: all behavior is gated behind feature flags and config; default settings preserve existing autoscaler behavior. Bridge is opt-in per-pool. No schema changes to billing pipelines.

References: Linear ENG-3421 (throughput stabilization), ENG-3499 (telemetry for borrowed capacity), SUP-1284 (customer incident that motivated bridge design).

release_notes: Introduce Stable Throughput Watcher: drift-aware estimator to reduce oscillation and unnecessary scale events.
Add Opportunistic Burst Bridger: safely borrow warm pool capacity for short spikes without changing tenant commitments.
Configurable via helm feature flags; rollout planned as canary-first.
